deadline.value: Apply by January 1, 2027 for Fall enrollment.
deadline.quote: WHEN DO I SUBMIT MY ONLINE APPLICATION? The deadline is: January 1 for fall enrollment

also.quote: CHEMISTRY - PH.D. | Deadline for Fall Enrollment January 1 for fall enrollment

gre_general.value: The GRE General Test is not required for Chemistry PhD admission.
gre_general.quote: DO I HAVE TO TAKE THE GRE EXAM? No, the GRE is not required.

also.quote: CHEMISTRY - PH.D. | GRE General Requirement No

gre_subject.value: The Chemistry GRE Subject Test is listed as optional.
gre_subject.quote: CHEMISTRY - PH.D. | Additional Requirements GRE Subject Test: optional

supervisor.value: First-year students complete two laboratory rotations in the fall semester and choose a research mentor in December.
supervisor.quote: First year students are required to perform two research lab rotations in the first semester to better familiarize themselves with the faculty and their research. Mentor selection is done in December, and all students are expected to start their research by the spring of their first year.

funding.value: Every admitted Chemistry PhD student receives a five-year CUNY Science Scholarship covering tuition, health benefits, and a $30,000/year living stipend.
funding.quote: Each student admitted for doctoral study in Chemistry is awarded a multi-year CUNY Science Scholarship which guarantees financial support for five full years of study, as long as the student remains in good academic standing and progresses on schedule in his/her doctoral research. The scholarship includes tuition, a $30,000/year living allowance, and low-cost health benefits through NYSHIP.

entry_route.value: Applicants enter directly with an undergraduate background in chemistry or a related science; no master's degree is required.
entry_route.quote: Unless specifically noted on our deadlines and requirements chart, you do not need to have a master's degree before you start a Ph.D. program.

also.quote: The ideal applicant to the Ph.D. program in Chemistry will have a strong undergraduate academic background and record of research accomplishments in chemistry or related experiential science.
